sentences.text:
Sri Kalyani Prasad Chakrabarty vs The State Of West Bengal &
Ors on 14 June, 2024

Author: Amrita Sinha
Bench: Amrita Sinha
 Ml-87
14.06.2024
Court No. 14
 Agm
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Constitutional Writ Jurisdiction
 Appellate Side
 W.P.A 27683 of 2023
 Sri Kalyani Prasad Chakrabarty
 -versus
 The State of West Bengal & Ors.
 Mr. Kartick Kumar Bhattacharya.
 Mr. Soumashree Dutta.
Ms. Papita Naskar.
... For the petitioner.
Mr. Shyamal Kumar Das.
Ms. Smita Pal.
Mr. Krishna Yadav.
... For the respondent no. 5.
Mr. Sumon Ghosh.
Ms. Munmun Tewary.
... For the State.
The petitioner, a septuagenarian widower, alleges that her elder daughter, the respondent no. 4 has driven him out from his house.
The house in question is recorded in the joint name of the petitioner and his wife, since deceased.
According to the petitioner, the respondent nos. 5 and 6 in conspiracy and in connivance with the respondent no. 4 drove out the petitioner from the house.
The petitioner intends to return to this house.
Complaint was lodged before the police.
Allegation is that the police did not take any step in response to the said complaint.

sentences.text: 1 Learned advocate representing the respondent no. 5 denies the allegation of the petitioner.
It has been submitted that the respondent no. 5 is a well-wisher of the respondent no. 4.

Apart from providing assistance to the respondent no. 4 for looking after the younger sister of the respondent no. 4 who is physically disabled and mentally unstable, the respondent no. 5 does not have any relationship with either the petitioner or his family members.

Learned advocate representing the State respondents relies upon the report forwarded by the Officer-in-Charge, Khardah Police Station signed on 19th December, 2023 wherefrom it appears that the complaint filed by the petitioner was diarised vide Khardah P.S. G.D.E. No. 2088 dated 30.04.2020.

The private respondent no. 4 also lodged a complaint which was diarised vide G.D.E.
376 dated 05.02.2021 and GDE No. 158 dated 02.03.2021.

The respondent no. 4 filed a complaint case before the Court resulting in registering Khardah P.S. Case No. 210 of 2021 dated 1st April,
2021 under Sections 323/354/379/420/406/506/120B IPC.
The said case was investigated and charge sheet has been filed.
In response to the complaint lodged by the petitioner the police submitted prosecution under Section 107 Cr.P.C. against the respondent no. 4.

Learned advocate for the State respondents has drawn attention of the Court to the statement of the respondent no. 4 recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
I have perused the same.
On a perusal of the said statement the Court is not inclined to immediately permit the petitioner to return to his own house.
Learned advocate representing the petitioner is directed to obtain instruction as to whether there is a separate room in the house with a separate entrance, which the petitioner may occupy.
The petitioner shall also make arrangement for taking charge of the medical bills and treatment of his younger daughter.
The respondent nos. 5 and 6 are restrained from interfering or meddling with the personal disputes between the father and the daughters.
The respondent nos. 5 and 6 are also restrained from in entering into the flat of the petitioner being flat no. D-06/102, Sodepur Peerless Nagar, 29F, B. T. Road, P.O. Panihati, P.S. Khardah.
Let the matter appear in the list on 24th June, 2024.

( Amrita Sinha, J.)
